source_evidence: The following chart shows the impact of three different fees on a $100,000 investment that grows 4% annually over 20 years. At the end of 20 years, the portfolio would be worth approximately $208,000. At the end of 20 years, the portfolio would be worth approximately $198,000. At the end of 20 years, the portfolio would be worth approximately $179,000.
answer: When comparing investment product fees, look at the ongoing annual fee and compare products on the same basis. The source’s hypothetical example holds the investment amount, growth rate, and time period constant: $100,000 growing 4% annually for 20 years. With a 0.25% annual fee, it would be worth approximately $208,000; with a 0.50% fee, approximately $198,000; and with a 1.00% fee, approximately $179,000. This example illustrates how different fees can affect a portfolio’s value over time. When evaluating products, ask how their fees and expenses compare, and also ask about purchase, sale, and account-maintenance fees.
